Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client.picker

Class PickerState

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client.picker.PickerState
public final class PickerState extends Object
In-world eye-placement authoring state, driven by the /sg CLI and the keyboard picker, which share this state. Creative-mode only; works in single-player and from a remote client alike — the operations that touch the server (mob freezing, export) go through the C2S picker packets and are re-authorized server-side. Workflow: choose a mob, pick a part to use as the coordinate frame, shape a current eye (position / rotation / properties), then save it to a flat, numbered eye list. Re-select a saved eye to adjust it in place; export sends the list, grouped by part, to the server to be written into the world datapack.

Client-only singleton (static state). Each saved eye remembers its own attach part, so the list can span multiple parts; export regroups by part into heads.

      public static boolean setCrossTarget(int oneBased)
      The CLI properties crosstarget <n> op: point the current eye's cross-eye behavior at the eye at 1-based list index oneBased (<= 0 clears it). The target must be a different eye that shares the current part — cross-eye is same-head only. Returns false if out of range, the edited eye itself, or on a different part.

    • resetOnDisconnect

      public static void resetOnDisconnect()
      Reset picker state to its construction state on disconnect, without sending anything — the connection may already be gone, and the server's own logout handling (PickerFreezeService.onPlayerLoggedOut(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer)) releases any frozen mob regardless.

      The authored drafts go too, along with targetType. They were authored against — and seeded from — the server we're leaving, and export would happily send them to the next server we join, writing one world's eye configs into another's datapack.
